description:
Hi! I'm Fathima Shaima, a Software Engineering graduate from Kandy, Sri Lanka, and I'm tackling the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge on my own.
I'll use Python, Pandas, and Scikit-learn to analyze NASA Earth data and find meaningful trends. I'll then present them in an interactive React dashboard.
This is a solo project, so I'm not recruiting members. I'm always happy to connect with other participants, share ideas, and learn from the community.
summary: Earth Trend Detective analyzes 146 years of NASA GISTEMP global surface temperature data (1880-2025) to show how fast Earth is warming and whether the change is speeding up. Using Python, Pandas and NumPy, I calculated linear warming trends for four periods, a 10-year rolling average and decade averages. Warming was +0.08°C per decade since 1880, rising to +0.16 since 1950, +0.21 since 1980 and +0.26 since 2000, about three times the long-term rate. 2024 is the warmest year in the dataset (+1.28°C above the 1951-1980 baseline). The results are shown in an interactive dashboard with a yearly chart, trend line, key statistics and a decade comparison, so anyone can explore the change without reading raw data. The project answers the challenge by showing what is changing (global temperature), how much (°C per decade), and how the rate has changed over time.
details:
What it does: Earth Trend Detective turns raw NASA temperature data into a clear picture of long-term warming. It shows what is changing (global surface temperature), how much (°C per decade), and how the rate has changed (0.08 since 1880 to 0.26 since 2000).

How it works: I load NASA GISTEMP annual anomalies (difference from the 1951-1980 average), fit linear trends for four periods, compute a 10-year rolling average and decade averages, and display them in an interactive dashboard where the start year can be changed.

Tools: Python, Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, JavaScript, HTML/CSS.

Impact: It helps students and the public see climate change in the data without technical knowledge.

Limits and next steps: The project uses one global variable. Future work: regional data, sea level, statistical significance tests, and forecasts.

AI use: AI assistance (Claude by Anthropic) was used to help write the analysis code, build the dashboard, create the demo video and slides, and draft this text. Created by Fathima Shaima, team Blue Marble Detective.
